components.description: Trust banner certifying AST equivalence and zero functional regressions.
components.html:
AST Equivalence Guarantee Verified Invariant

narrative.overview:
CouchPilot is an autonomous repository housekeeping agent with a review workbench engineered for high-trust code verification. The aesthetic philosophy is rooted in the calm, unembellished clarity of a precision laboratory instrument: dense yet immediately scanable, restrained, and completely devoid of decorative marketing tropes such as gradient text, artificial glassmorphism, or ambient neon halos.

Every visual decision reflects the solemnity of automated code modification: maintainers and judges must verify that default branches were protected and that zero functional regressions were introduced. Grounded on an unbleached oat substrate (#F7F5F0), deep slate typography (#1F2A33), and hairline architectural dividers (#E2DCCF), the system directs attention solely toward AST verification guarantees, review branches, and syntax-highlighted diffs.
keyCharacteristics: Calm, High-Contrast Readability: Natural oat ground with tinted charcoal body text preserves focus during deep technical diff audits.
Strict AST-Equivalence Transparency: Verification status is treated as an immutable certificate of safety rather than an incidental badge.
Semantic Accent Discipline: Interactive triggers, operational statuses, and diff additions operate under distinct, non-overlapping color roles.
Zero Decorative Noise: Lucide SVG line icons with uniform 2px stroke width; strictly no raw emojis anywhere in the interface.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Imperial Plum is reserved strictly for primary deliberate actions and focus rings, occupying <=5% of screen surface area. Its rarity guarantees immediate visual hierarchy.

rules.name: The Contrast Invariant Rule
rules.body: White text is strictly forbidden on Tangerine, Butter, and Red backgrounds. Badges in these states must use Deep Slate (#1F2A33) text on pale tinted backgrounds to satisfy WCAG AA contrast ratios.

rules.name: The No-Gradient Rule
rules.body: Plum and Marine must never be blended into a gradient. Each represents an independent semantic state (Deliberate Action vs Navigational/Operational Focus).

rules.name: The Monospace Honesty Rule
rules.body: Monospace typography is strictly reserved for code, AST nodes, git commit hashes, file paths, branch names, and tabular execution metrics. It must never be used as a decorative costume for general copy.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: All numerical metrics, token counters, and elapsed time durations must declare font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums to eliminate layout jitter during live updates.

rules.name: The Zero-Halo Rule
rules.body: Soft colored glows and zero-blur hard block drop shadows are strictly prohibited. Shadows exist only to establish spatial elevation above the ground plane.

rules.name: The Hairline Discipline Rule
rules.body: Container borders must never exceed 1px. Thick decorative side-tab borders on list cards are strictly banned.

dos: Do use Outfit for UI interface copy and JetBrains Mono for commit hashes, paths, and diffs.
Do enforce WCAG AA contrast standards by using Deep Slate text on low-contrast status backgrounds (Tangerine and Butter).
Do render icons using Lucide SVG line icons with a consistent 2px stroke width.
Do format diff additions in #236B3E with #EBF5EE background, and deletions in #B83227 with #FCEBEA background.
Do display the AST Equivalence Guarantee prominently on all diff inspection views.
donts: Don't use raw emojis anywhere in the UI, templates, logs, CLI output, or commit messages.
Don't combine Imperial Plum and Deep Marine into a gradient.
Don't use colored border-left accents thicker than 1px on list cards or table rows.
Don't put white text on yellow, orange, or red badges.
Don't add decorative blur, glow halos, or animations beyond functional state transitions.
